label: C-01
title: FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges silently voids every outstanding antimatter claim, and Antimatter exposes no view of its own authorisation status
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: Every outstanding antimatter token becomes permanently inert on one call from a principal who is not Antimatter's owner and may not be reasoning about antimatter at all. Antimatter is a reward token with no purchase price, so no capital is destroyed - but the entire outstanding claim is.
attackPath: 1. FlaxToken's owner uses the documented global kill switch revokeAllMintPrivileges (mintVersion++).
2. There is no per-minter event and no view on either contract, so nothing signals that Antimatter has been de-authorised.

3. Annihilation is silently dead while ordinary minting still works after re-setMinter on the minter alone; off-chain UIs still see a configured, registered, non-paused system because toStableAmount still returns successfully.
4. Recovery requires re-setMinter on BOTH contracts; forgetting Antimatter leaves the failure latent.
classification.assumptions: FlaxToken owner and Antimatter owner may be different parties, and nothing requires them to coordinate.

justification: Centralization/upstream-privilege finding, filed C-01 at Low. NOT a malicious-owner vector - it is the observability and two-contract-recovery gap around a legitimate emergency lever that makes it a Law-3 footgun: a competent, non-malicious phUSD owner would be surprised that a global kill switch also voids an unrelated token's entire outstanding claim and that recovery needs two contracts. Not Medium: the action is deliberate and emergency-scoped, and antimatter carries no purchase price. Deliberately NOT collapsed with C-02 - same trust structure, different mitigations (an authorisation view + runbook vs an own-owner pause flag).
recommendation: Expose a view on Antimatter reporting whether it is currently an authorised, current-version phUSD minter, so the condition is observable without simulating an annihilation.
Document the two-contract re-authorisation requirement in the incident runbook.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: Antimatter's entire value depends on a mint authorisation held by a third, independent owner (FlaxToken), revocable wholesale via mintVersion++ with no per-minter event and no view on either contract.
additionalContext.impact: Every outstanding antimatter token becomes permanently inert on one call from a principal who is not antimatter's owner and may not be reasoning about antimatter at all. Recovery requires re-setMinter on BOTH contracts; forgetting Antimatter leaves annihilation silently dead while ordinary minting works, and off-chain UIs still see a configured, registered, non-paused system (toStableAmount still returns successfully).
additionalContext.footgunTest: Law 3 - a competent, non-malicious phUSD owner using the documented global kill switch would be surprised that it also voids an unrelated token's entire outstanding claim, and that recovery requires re-authorising two contracts. In scope.
additionalContext.stalePinCaveat: lib/flax-token-v2 @ f5300117 is ~9 months old (2025-11-20) and there is no top-level sibling to cross-read. DIFF-ONLY claim about that tree.
additionalContext.severityRationale: QA/Low, Law-3 footgun. Not Medium: the action is deliberate and emergency-scoped, and antimatter is a reward token with no purchase price.

mergeAction: Kept separate from DEDUP-012 (CODE-009 'no kill switch of its own'). Verified before deciding: both observe that Antimatter's control levers belong to independent principals, but the root causes and mitigations differ - DEDUP-011 is 'a global revoke by a third principal is a silent, unobservable liability repudiation' (fix: expose an authorisation view + two-contract re-auth runbook); DEDUP-012 is 'Antimatter's own owner has no proportionate lever at all' (fix: an annihilationPaused flag). Neither mitigation implies the other.
